mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in FEDFUNDS above 3% in the month preceding the forecast period is associated with higher S&P 500 20-day forward returns due to reduced real interest rates encouraging equity investment.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 3% in the preceding month
regime_hint: tightening phase of the Fed funds rate
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher than the 30-day moving average of the same period in the prior month (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Rising monthly PAYEMS (labor market strength) coinciding with UNRATE below 3.5% is associated with positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns as strong labor demand supports corporate earnings growth.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE < 3.5% in the current month
regime_hint: labor market strengthening with low unemployment
failure_condition: Rank IC < 0.05 over the 60-day horizon for all months with similar labor conditions.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly rise in HOUST (industrial production) above 1% for two consecutive months predicts positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns as it signals accelerating economic activity.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by >1% in month t and again in month t+1
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in all months meeting the production signal.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in INDPRO (industrial production index) below 104.5 over the prior 3 months predicts negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns as weak supply growth raises recession risk.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during INDPRO < 104.5 periods.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in CPIAUCSL (inflation) below 297 over the prior month triggers a positive S&P 500 5-day forward return as markets anticipate lower rate hike likelihood.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses below 297 in the previous month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are flat or negative during the inflation decline period.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in PAYEMS and UNRATE above 3.5% indicate labor market tightening, which is associated with negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns due to wage growth concerns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 3.5% and UNRATE > 3.5% in the same month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in such labor market conditions.

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in GDPC1 (GDP) over the last 6 months predicts negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns as weak aggregate demand suppresses earnings growth.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.05) during GDPC1 decline.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly increases in RSAFS (retail sales) above 680,000 suggest strengthening consumer demand, which is associated with positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not positive in 4 out of 5 consecutive months with similar RSAFS trends.
